person.persName: bcom ldan rigs pa'i ral gri
person.note: On his career, see [KHA9ZVGP]: 3-8. The dates 1227-1305 are known from the biography (see work (ID:7016)) composed by his student bSam gtan bzang po (ID:4005) ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3). His name in religion was Dar ma rgyal mtshan or Chos kyi rgyal mtshan ([FZ6N88AU]: 406) - the name Chos kyi rgyal mtshan is given as his "real name" (mtshan dngos) in a homage by Rong ston ([KM47ZZDJ]: 657 and n. 62). The majority of the colophons of his works name him "bCom ldan ral gri," a few "Rigs/Rig pa’i ral gri" or just "Ral gri." Schwabland's discussion of the variants “Rigs pa” and “Rig pa” does not come to a definite conclusion as to which is the correct spelling ([CTQMVBPR]: 2-3). He was born as the son of a local wealthy headman, the fourth of five sons and his birth is reported to have been foretold by Śākyaśrībhadra (ID:6418) when he was invited by Ral gri's paternal uncle ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3).

person.persName: btsun pa grags pa rgyal mtshan
person.note: The "btsun pa grags pa rgyal mtshan" who wrote down (ID:4794) could be Ze'u grags pa rgyal mtshan/Chu mig pa grags pa rgyal mtshan (ID:6133), a teacher of sKyo ston. (See Skyo ston smon lam tshul khrims kyi rnam thar in [LRSRMBWG]: 349a2). According to [NTGHCZA8]: 65, n. 145, this Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan could be the "Grags rgyal" mentioned in Sangs rgyas sgom pa's biography. In fact this “slob dpon Grags rgyal” bestowed on Sangs rgyas sgom pa (1179-1250) similar teachings to those that we find listed as passed from Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan to sKyo ston. The gDams ngag mdzod reports a Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan in the transmission of the white Jambhala (dzam dkar) that runs thus: spyan ras gzigs| rgya brtson 'gris seng ge| nag tsho tshul rgyal| rong pa phyag sor ba| pu to ba| sha ra ba| gtum ston pa| chu mig pa grags pa rgyal mtshan| gro ston bdud rtsi grags| zhang ston chos blo| mchims nam mkha' grags […] (the list reaches Tāranātha and then refers to a lineage given previously for the following lineage holders, so it would seem that the source for this lineage is given somewhere in Tāranātha's writings). If this is the case, this Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan would be already a student of the first abbot of sNar thang gTum ston grags pa (1106-1166). This would be possible only if this Grags pa rgyal mtshan was born around the late 1150s and taught sKyo ston when he was already about 70 years of age.

person.persName: snar thang mkhan chen nyi ma rgyal mtshan
dge ba'i bshes bsnyen bla ma blo gros rgyal mtshan dpal bzang po
tshad ma'i skyes bu bsod nams mgon
person.note:
In the teaching lineage of Zang rings grags pa dar ma tshul khrims (ID:4011) ([8GL7ZT7Y]: 25, translated from [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15a3). See [CTAI38G9]: 924 on his nicknames "tshad ma'i skyes bu" and "rigs thigs pa," and his dates, proposed to be ca. 1235-1315, considering that he was teaching at Khro phu in 1307 and taught until his 83rd year.
[CTAI38G9]: 928 defends the idea that "Tshad ma'i skyes bu" is bSod nams mgon po and not Don grub dpal, another teacher of Bu ston (ID:5999).
